experiences.name: Annapurna Base Camp Trek
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic multi-day trek to Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130m, passing through rhododendron forests, terraced fields, and traditional Gurung villages. Witness breathtaking panoramic views of Annapurna I, Machapuchare, and Hiunchuli peaks. This is the crown jewel of Himalayan trekking experiences.

experiences.name: Poon Hill Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Rise before dawn and hike to Poon Hill viewpoint at 3,210m for one of the most spectacular sunrises in the Himalayas. Watch golden light illuminate the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri mountain ranges in a stunning alpenglow display. A relatively accessible hike suitable for most fitness levels.
experiences.location: Ghorepani, Poon Hill, Annapurna Conservation Area

experiences.name: Mardi Himal Trek
experiences.description: Explore the lesser-known Mardi Himal trail, a hidden gem offering solitude and raw Himalayan beauty away from the crowds. Trek through dense bamboo and rhododendron forests, high alpine meadows, and enjoy close-up views of Machapuchare (Fishtail Mountain). A rewarding off-the-beaten-path adventure.
experiences.location: Mardi Himal, Eastern Annapurna Conservation Area

experiences.name: Gurung Village Cultural Homestay & Nature Walk
experiences.description: Stay overnight in an authentic Gurung village and join a guided nature walk with a local elder who shares knowledge of medicinal plants, traditional farming, and Himalayan wildlife. Enjoy a home-cooked dal bhat meal and learn about the indigenous culture and animist traditions of the mountain communities.

experiences.name: Jhinu Danda Natural Hot Springs Soak
experiences.description: After days of strenuous trekking, reward your tired muscles with a soak in the natural riverside hot springs at Jhinu Danda. Set along the Modi Khola river surrounded by lush jungle and mountain scenery, these geothermal pools offer a deeply restorative and uniquely Himalayan nature experience.
experiences.location: Jhinu Danda, Modi Khola River, Annapurna Conservation Area

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Annapurna, Nepal
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Annapurna Sanctuary, Annapurna Conservation Area Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 13:00. Clear immigration, collect baggage, and exchange currency at the airport (rates are reasonable here). Take a pre-paid taxi or local bus to Thamel, the budget traveler hub. Check into a budget guesthouse in Thamel (~$8-12/night). Rest and freshen up after the flight.
day_by_day.evening: Short orientation walk around Thamel neighborhood. Visit a local gear shop to rent or buy any missing trekking equipment (poles, sleeping bag liners, etc.). Explore the narrow alleys of Thamel and pick up any last-minute supplies for the trek.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane
meals.lunch: Grab a quick dal bhat or momo at a local Thamel eatery (~$2-3) after settling in
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local Thamel restaurant - try Thakali Kitchen or similar for authentic Nepali dal bhat set (~$4-5)

day_by_day.notes: Obtain your ACAP (Annapurna Conservation Area Permit) and TIMS card today if offices are still open, or first thing tomorrow morning. ACAP costs ~$30 USD and TIMS ~$20 USD. Drink plenty of water and rest early to prepare for early morning departure tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early at 6:00 AM. Collect permits if not done yesterday (ACAP and TIMS cards from Nepal Tourism Board office, open from 9 AM). Head to Kathmandu's tourist bus park in Thamel by 7:00 AM. Board a tourist bus or local bus to Pokhara (~7-8 hours, $7-10 for tourist bus or $4-5 for local bus).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Pokhara around 2:00-3:00 PM. Check into a budget guesthouse near Lakeside area (~$6-10/night). Drop your heavy city bag at the guesthouse (arrange storage). Repack your trekking backpack with only essentials. Visit a gear shop if anything is still needed.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Phewa Lake at Lakeside (Baidam). Watch the sunset over the Annapurna range from the lakeside promenade - a stunning free experience. Browse local shops and soak in the mountain town atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at Thamel guesthouse or a nearby bakery (~$2-3)
meals.lunch: Pack lunch or eat at a roadside dhaba during the bus stop break (~$2-3)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat at a local Lakeside restaurant in Pokhara (~$3-5) - try Moondance Restaurant or a local Nepali eatery

day_by_day.notes: Double-check your trekking permits are in order. Confirm your bus ticket or jeep to Nayapul or Phedi for tomorrow morning. Carry enough Nepali rupees as ATMs become scarce on the trek. Charge all electronics tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up at 5:30 AM. Eat a hearty breakfast and take a local bus or shared jeep from Pokhara to Nayapul (~1.5 hours, ~$2-3). Begin trekking from Nayapul. Follow the well-marked trail through Birethanti (permit checkpoint - have your ACAP and TIMS ready). Trek through terraced farmland and lush forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking through Hile and Ulleri direction. Enjoy the scenic Modi Khola river valley. The trail climbs steadily through rhododendron and oak forests. Reach Tikhedhunga (1,540m) by early afternoon after approximately 4-5 hours of trekking.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a basic teahouse/lodge in Tikhedhunga (~$2-5/night, often free with meal commitment). Rest your legs and soak in the mountain village atmosphere. Chat with fellow trekkers and share trail tips. Enjoy the peaceful sounds of the river below.

meals.breakfast: Oats porridge or eggs and toast at Pokhara guesthouse (~$2-3)
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or dal bhat at a teahouse along the trail (~$3-4)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat set at the Tikhedhunga teahouse (~$4-5) - the classic trekker's fuel meal

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance: approximately 10-12 km, 4-5 hours. Tikhedhunga sits at the base of the famous 3,000+ stone staircase leading to Ulleri. Stay hydrated and pace yourself - this is just the beginning. Trekking poles are very helpful for the steps tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Early start at 6:30 AM. The day begins with the legendary stone staircase climb to Ulleri (2,050m) - approximately 3,000 steps! Take your time and enjoy the views back down the valley. Pass through Ulleri village and continue upward through dense rhododendron forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue climbing through Banthanti (2,250m) and Nangethanti. The forest becomes increasingly beautiful with moss-covered trees and mountain views opening up. Arrive at Ghorepani (2,860m) by early afternoon. The iconic Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges come into view.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a teahouse in Ghorepani (~$2-5/night). Warm up with a cup of hot lemon tea or ginger tea by the fire. Watch the alpenglow on the Annapurna range as the sun sets. Set your alarm for 4:30 AM for the Poon Hill sunrise hike tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Porridge with honey or chapati with eggs at Tikhedhunga teahouse (~$3-4)
meals.lunch: Vegetable fried rice or noodle soup at Ulleri teahouse (~$3-5)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or pasta at Ghorepani teahouse (~$4-6) - eat well to fuel tomorrow's early hike

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance: approximately 11 km, 5-6 hours with significant elevation gain. This is one of the toughest days of the trek. Go slow, breathe deeply, and drink plenty of water. Altitude awareness begins here - if you feel headache or nausea, rest and acclimatize. Ghorepani has several teahouses - shop around for the best deal.

day_by_day.date: Day 5 - 2027-10-19 (Poon Hill Sunrise & Trek to Tadapani)
day_by_day.morning: Wake up at 4:30 AM. Hike up to Poon Hill (3,210m) by headlamp - takes about 45 minutes. Watch one of the most spectacular sunrises in the Himalayas with 360-degree views of Dhaulagiri, Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Machhapuchhre (Fishtail), and more. Return to Ghorepani for breakfast by 8:00 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: After breakfast, trek from Ghorepani toward Tadapani via Deurali. The trail passes through stunning rhododendron forests (these bloom brilliantly in spring). Enjoy views of the Annapurna Sanctuary direction. Arrive at Tadapani (2,630m) by early afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into a teahouse in Tadapani. The village offers excellent views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli. Rest and recover from the morning's early start. Journal your experiences or simply sit and marvel at the mountain panorama.

meals.breakfast: Hot tea/coffee at Poon Hill viewpoint (vendors set up early, ~$1-2), then full breakfast at Ghorepani teahouse (~$3-4)
meals.lunch: Snacks and energy bars on the trail, or a quick stop at Deurali teahouse (~$3-4)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or vegetable curry at Tadapani teahouse (~$4-5)

day_by_day.notes: Poon Hill entry fee: ~$3 USD. Trek distance today: approximately 10 km, 4-5 hours (excluding Poon Hill). Tadapani is a quieter stop than Ghorepani and offers beautiful forest surroundings. The rhododendron forests are particularly magical in October light.

day_by_day.morning: Start trekking at 7:00 AM from Tadapani. The trail descends through beautiful forest to Gurjung and then climbs again. Enjoy the changing vegetation and increasing views of the Annapurna Sanctuary entrance. The trail offers stunning perspectives of Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Mountain).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Chomrong (2,170m), a large Gurung village that serves as the gateway to the Annapurna Sanctuary. Arrive by early afternoon. Explore the village, visit the small monastery, and enjoy the incredible views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli directly ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into a teahouse in Chomrong. This is the last major village before the restricted sanctuary zone. Stock up on any supplies needed (snacks, water purification tablets). The village has better facilities than upcoming stops. Enjoy the warm community atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes with honey or eggs at Tadapani teahouse (~$3-4)
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or fried rice at a trail teahouse (~$3-5)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat set at Chomrong teahouse (~$5-6) - slightly pricier as you go higher

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance: approximately 12 km, 5-6 hours with significant ups and downs. Chomrong has a permit checkpoint - have your ACAP card ready. Buy extra snacks here as prices increase significantly higher up. Water from here should be treated or boiled. The village has a wonderful community feel with Gurung culture on display.

day_by_day.morning: Begin trekking early from Chomrong. Descend the famous Chomrong stone staircase to Chomrong Khola (river) and then ascend to Sinuwa (2,360m). The trail enters the bamboo and rhododendron forest zone - a magical transition. Keep eyes open for wildlife including Himalayan tahrs and various bird species.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through Bamboo (2,310m) - a small settlement surrounded by dense bamboo forest. The trail follows the Modi Khola river deeper into the sanctuary. Arrive at Dovan (2,600m) by afternoon. The valley narrows dramatically and the atmosphere becomes more remote and wild.
day_by_day.evening: Rest at Dovan teahouse. The sound of the river and the towering valley walls create an immersive mountain experience. The stars at night are spectacular due to minimal light pollution. Prepare for higher altitudes ahead.

meals.breakfast: Porridge or Tibetan bread with jam at Chomrong teahouse (~$3-4)
meals.lunch: Simple noodle soup or dal bhat at Sinuwa or Bamboo teahouse (~$4-6)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or pasta at Dovan teahouse (~$5-7) - prices continue to rise with altitude

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance: approximately 10 km, 5-6 hours. This section enters the Annapurna Sanctuary proper - a UNESCO-recognized conservation area. No open fires are permitted. Respect wildlife and stay on marked trails. Altitude sickness awareness is important - drink 3-4 liters of water daily. The bamboo forest section is absolutely stunning.

day_by_day.morning: This is the big day! Start early at 6:00 AM. Trek from Dovan through Himalaya Hotel (2,920m) and Hinku Cave (3,170m). The valley opens up dramatically as you gain altitude. Pass through Deurali (3,230m) - the cloud zone where weather can change rapidly. The landscape becomes increasingly alpine and dramatic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the steady climb to Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC) at 3,700m. Stop for lunch and enjoy the incredible 360-degree mountain views. After resting, make the final push to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) at 4,130m. Arrive at the sacred amphitheater surrounded by 7,000m+ peaks.
day_by_day.evening: You are now at the heart of the Annapurna Sanctuary! Check into your teahouse at ABC. The views of Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Gangapurna, Hiunchuli, and Machhapuchhre are absolutely overwhelming. Watch the sunset paint the peaks in golden and pink hues - a once-in-a-lifetime experience.

meals.breakfast: Hearty porridge and eggs at Dovan teahouse (~$4-5)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or noodle soup at Machhapuchhre Base Camp (~$6-8)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or pasta at ABC teahouse (~$7-10) - worth every rupee at this altitude and location

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance: approximately 14 km, 7-8 hours with significant altitude gain. This is the highest point of the trek at 4,130m. Altitude sickness is a real concern - symptoms include headache, nausea, dizziness, and fatigue. If symptoms are severe, descend immediately. Drink plenty of water. Temperatures drop significantly at night - ensure you have warm layers. Set alarm for 5:00 AM for sunrise.

day_by_day.morning: Wake at 5:00 AM for the most spectacular sunrise of your life. Watch the first light illuminate the ring of Himalayan giants surrounding you - Annapurna I, II, III, IV, South, Gangapurna, Hiunchuli, and the sacred Machhapuchhre. Spend the morning exploring the base camp area and soaking in the sanctuary atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin descent after a late breakfast. The descent is much faster than the ascent. Pass back through Machhapuchhre Base Camp, Deurali, and Hinku Cave. The descent through the bamboo forest zone is beautiful. Continue down to Bamboo (2,310m) by afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into Bamboo teahouse. Your legs will feel the descent but the lower altitude brings more oxygen and easier breathing. Celebrate your achievement of reaching ABC with fellow trekkers over dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hot tea and toast or porridge at ABC teahouse (~$4-5)
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or snacks on the trail (~$4-6)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat at Bamboo teahouse (~$5-6) - a well-deserved hearty meal

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance: approximately 16 km descent, 6-7 hours. Descending is easier on lungs but harder on knees - trekking poles are very helpful. Take your time on steep sections. The lower altitude will help you sleep much better tonight. You may feel a surge of energy as you descend to lower, oxygen-richer elevations.

day_by_day.morning: Start trekking from Bamboo at 7:00 AM. Re-ascend through Sinuwa and back up to Chomrong. The views of the Annapurna range from Chomrong are still breathtaking even on the return journey. Take a different trail variation if possible for new perspectives.
day_by_day.afternoon: From Chomrong, take the trail down toward Jhinu Danda (1,760m). This small village is famous for its natural hot springs by the Modi Khola river. Arrive by early afternoon and check into a teahouse.
day_by_day.evening: The highlight of the day - soak in the natural hot springs at Jhinu Danda! The hot spring pools by the river are the perfect reward for your trekking efforts. The warm mineral waters soothe tired muscles beautifully. Entry fee is minimal (~$1-2). Watch the stars emerge as you soak.

meals.breakfast: Tibetan bread with honey or eggs at Bamboo teahouse (~$3-5)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or fried rice at Chomrong (~$5-6)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or noodle soup at Jhinu Danda teahouse (~$4-5)

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance: approximately 12 km, 5-6 hours. Jhinu Danda hot springs are one of the most rewarding stops on the entire Annapurna Circuit - do not miss them! The springs are a 15-minute walk down from the village to the river. Bring flip flops and a towel. The teahouses here are simple but comfortable.

day_by_day.morning: One final soak in the hot springs at sunrise if you wake early enough (optional). Start trekking by 7:30 AM from Jhinu Danda. The trail continues down through New Bridge and Chhomrong area toward the valley floor. The terrain is lush and green with terraced fields.
day_by_day.afternoon: Trek through Siwai and Matathanti back to Nayapul. Total trekking time approximately 4-5 hours. Reach Nayapul and arrange a local bus or shared jeep back to Pokhara (~1.5 hours, ~$2-3). Arrive in Pokhara by mid-afternoon. Check into Lakeside guesthouse.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate completing the Annapurna Sanctuary Trek! Enjoy a proper shower, clean clothes, and the comforts of Pokhara. Stroll along Phewa Lake at sunset. Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner to celebrate your achievement.

meals.breakfast: Porridge or eggs at Jhinu Danda teahouse (~$3-4)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or snacks at a trail teahouse near Nayapul (~$3-5)
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at a Lakeside restaurant in Pokhara - try momos, thukpa, or a Nepali set meal (~$5-8)

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance: approximately 10-12 km, 4-5 hours to Nayapul. You have successfully completed the Annapurna Sanctuary Trek! Total trekking: approximately 9 days, covering 100+ km with maximum altitude of 4,130m. Get a massage in Pokhara tonight - many budget massage centers offer Nepali or Thai massage for ~$8-12/hour.

day_by_day.morning: Well-deserved rest morning! Sleep in and have a leisurely breakfast. Visit the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) - hike up or take a short boat ride across Phewa Lake and walk up (~$1-2 boat fee). The pagoda offers panoramic views of Pokhara, the lake, and the Annapurna range.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the International Mountain Museum in Pokhara (~$5 entry) - an excellent museum dedicated to Himalayan mountaineering history and culture. Alternatively, rent a rowboat on Phewa Lake (~$5-7/hour) for a peaceful paddle with mountain reflections. Visit Devi's Falls and the Gupteshwor Cave nearby (~$1-2 each).
day_by_day.evening: Browse the Lakeside market for souvenirs - Nepali handicrafts, Thangka paintings, pashmina scarves, and trekking gear. Bargain respectfully. Enjoy a final Pokhara evening with lake views and mountain backdrop.

meals.breakfast: Western-style breakfast at a Lakeside cafe - granola, yogurt, fresh fruit (~$3-5)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local Nepali restaurant - try Thakali cuisine (~$4-6)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or try local Newari cuisine at a budget restaurant (~$4-6)

day_by_day.notes: This is your recovery day - listen to your body. Many trekkers get massages, do laundry, and simply rest. Pokhara has excellent budget cafes with fast WiFi if you need to catch up on communications. The Lakeside area has a great atmosphere with many fellow trekkers sharing stories.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Pokhara guesthouse. Take a morning tourist bus or local bus back to Kathmandu (~7-8 hours, $7-10 tourist bus). Alternatively, take a domestic flight (~$80-100, 25 minutes) if budget allows - book in advance with Yeti Airlines or Buddha Air. Enjoy the scenic mountain views from the bus or plane.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Kathmandu. Check into a Thamel guesthouse (~$8-12/night). Head to the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Pashupatinath Temple area for an afternoon visit. Watch the Aarti ceremony on the banks of the Bagmati River - a profound Hindu spiritual experience (free to observe from the riverbank).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Thamel's vibrant streets for last-minute shopping. Visit a local bookshop for books on Nepal and Himalayan trekking. Enjoy a final Kathmandu evening with live Nepali folk music at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast before departure at Pokhara (~$2-3)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the bus or roadside dhaba stop (~$2-3)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Thamel - try Krishnarpan restaurant for budget Nepali thali or a local eatery (~$4-7)

day_by_day.notes: Book your return bus ticket the evening before or early morning. Tourist buses depart from Pokhara tourist bus park. If flying, Pokhara Airport is a short taxi ride from Lakeside (~$3-5). Keep your trekking permits as souvenirs - they make great memories. Start consolidating your luggage for the return journey home.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to Boudhanath Stupa - one of the largest Buddhist stupas in the world and a UNESCO World Heritage Site (free to walk around the outer area, small fee to enter the stupa area ~$3). Walk the kora (circumambulation) with pilgrims and monks. Visit nearby Kopan Monastery area for peaceful reflection.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Swayambhunath Temple (Monkey Temple) - a short taxi or walk from Thamel (~$1-2 entry). Climb the 365 steps for panoramic Kathmandu Valley views. Watch the playful monkeys and enjoy the Buddhist and Hindu religious art. Return to Thamel for final packing and any last souvenir shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Nepal! Treat yourself to a slightly splurge-worthy farewell meal at a rooftop restaurant in Thamel with Himalayan views. Reflect on the incredible 14-day journey. Head to Tribhuvan International Airport with plenty of time (arrive 3 hours before international departure).

meals.breakfast: Nepali breakfast at guesthouse or local cafe - sel roti with yogurt and tea (~$2-3)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local Thamel restaurant - momos and thukpa (~$3-5)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a Thamel rooftop restaurant - splurge on a full Nepali set meal or try yak steak (~$8-12)

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary estimate for 14 days: Permits (ACAP + TIMS): ~$50, Accommodation: ~$70-100 (mix of guesthouses and teahouses), Food: ~$150-180, Transport: ~$40-60, Activities/entry fees: ~$20-30, Miscellaneous/souvenirs: ~$30-50. Total estimated budget: $360-470 USD excluding international flights. Namaste and safe travels! Nepal will stay in your heart forever.

trip_options.title: Classic Annapurna, Nepal Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Annapurna Sanctuary, Annapurna Conservation Area Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and transfer to your hotel in Pokhara via private tourist bus or shared jeep (approximately 6-7 hours) or take a 25-minute domestic flight to Pokhara if budget allows. Settle into accommodation and rest.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Lakeside (Phewa Tal) promenade in Pokhara, browse local shops, and soak in the relaxed atmosphere. Enjoy views of the lake at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or grab a quick snack at Kathmandu airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a roadside dhaba (local eatery) en route — try dal bhat or momos for NPR 200-400
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range lakeside restaurant in Pokhara such as Moondance Restaurant or OR2K — try Nepali thali or pasta for NPR 600-900

day_by_day.notes: Since flight arrives at 13:00, Day 1 is primarily a travel and transit day. Book your Pokhara transfer in advance. Ensure TIMS card and Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP) are arranged either online or at the TAAN office in Pokhara the next morning.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the TAAN/TIMS office and Annapurna Conservation Area Project (ACAP) office in Pokhara to obtain trekking permits. Then visit the International Mountain Museum to learn about Himalayan history, culture, and the Annapurna range.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a boat ride on Phewa Lake to the Tal Barahi Temple on the island. Afterward, visit the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) via a short hike for panoramic views of Pokhara, the lake, and the Annapurna massif.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Lakeside bazaar, pick up any last-minute trekking gear or supplies. Enjoy a relaxed dinner and rest early to prepare for the trek.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local bakery — try eggs, toast, and coffee for NPR 300-500
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a lakeside café — try a sandwich or spring rolls for NPR 400-600
meals.dinner: Dinner at Busy Bee Café or Caffe Concerto — try wood-fired pizza or Nepali curry for NPR 700-1000

day_by_day.notes: TIMS card costs approximately USD 10 and ACAP permit costs NPR 3000. Carry passport-sized photos and your passport. Pack your trekking bag tonight — aim for under 10 kg for a comfortable trek.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast and take a tourist bus or private jeep from Pokhara to Nayapul (1.5-2 hours). Begin the trek from Nayapul through the Modi Khola valley, passing through terraced fields and small villages to Tikhedhunga (1,540m). Approx 3-4 hours trekking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Tikhedhunga up the famous stone staircase to Ulleri (1,960m), a challenging but rewarding ascent through rhododendron forests. Arrive at Ulleri and check into a teahouse.
day_by_day.evening: Relax on the teahouse terrace with views of the Annapurna South and Hiunchuli peaks. Interact with fellow trekkers and local villagers. Rest early.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Pokhara hotel — eggs, toast, porridge for NPR 400-600
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or noodle soup at a teahouse in Tikhedhunga for NPR 400-600
meals.dinner: Hearty dal bhat set at Ulleri teahouse — all-you-can-eat for NPR 500-700

day_by_day.notes: The Tikhedhunga to Ulleri section involves approximately 3,000 stone steps — take it slow and stay hydrated. October is peak trekking season so teahouses will be busy; book ahead if possible or arrive early to secure rooms.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for sunrise views over the Annapurna range from Ulleri. Begin trekking through dense rhododendron and oak forests to Ghorepani (2,860m). The trail is relatively gradual and scenic. Approx 3-4 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Ghorepani and check in. Explore the village and acclimatize. Take a short optional hike to the edge of the village for panoramic Himalayan views including Dhaulagiri and Annapurna South.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset views from Ghorepani if weather permits. Warm up with ginger lemon honey tea at the teahouse. Attend a short cultural interaction or simply rest and journal.

meals.breakfast: Porridge with honey and dried fruits at Ulleri teahouse for NPR 300-500
meals.lunch: Garlic soup and fried rice at a trail teahouse en route for NPR 400-600
meals.dinner: Vegetable curry with rice and lentils at Ghorepani teahouse for NPR 500-700

day_by_day.notes: Ghorepani is the base for the famous Poon Hill sunrise hike. Set your alarm for 4:30 AM the next morning. The teahouse will likely prepare an early breakfast or packed snacks. Temperatures drop significantly at night — layer up.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up at 4:30 AM and hike to Poon Hill (3,210m) — approximately 45 minutes to 1 hour. Witness one of the most spectacular sunrises in the Himalayas with views of Dhaulagiri, Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Machhapuchhre (Fishtail), and more. Return to Ghorepani for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Trek from Ghorepani through rhododendron forests to Tadapani (2,630m), a beautiful trail with continuous mountain views. Approx 3-4 hours. Check in and rest.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the peaceful forested surroundings of Tadapani. Watch for wildlife including Himalayan pheasants and langur monkeys. Relax and recover.

meals.breakfast: Hot tea/coffee at Poon Hill viewpoint (vendors set up stalls) and full breakfast back at Ghorepani teahouse — eggs, toast, porridge for NPR 400-600
meals.lunch: Light snack or noodle soup at a trail stop for NPR 300-500
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or pasta at Tadapani teahouse for NPR 500-700

day_by_day.notes: Poon Hill entry fee is NPR 100. Dress in warm layers for the pre-dawn hike — temperatures can be near freezing. Carry a headlamp. The trail to Tadapani passes through beautiful moss-draped forests — one of the most scenic sections of the route.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Tadapani down through dense forests to Chhomrong (2,170m), a large Gurung village with stunning views of Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre. The trail descends steeply and then climbs back up. Approx 4-5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Chhomrong and check into a well-appointed teahouse. Explore the village, visit the local Gurung cultural center, and enjoy the views. Chhomrong is the last major village before entering the Annapurna Sanctuary.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a hot shower (available at most Chhomrong teahouses), do laundry if needed, and relax. Chat with trekkers heading in both directions for trail conditions updates.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes with honey and tea at Tadapani teahouse for NPR 350-500
meals.lunch: Lunch at a teahouse in Sinuwa or along the trail — try macaroni soup or fried rice for NPR 400-600
meals.dinner: Apple pie and dal bhat at Chhomrong teahouse — Chhomrong is famous for its apple products for NPR 600-800

day_by_day.notes: Stock up on snacks, chocolate, and essentials in Chhomrong as prices increase significantly higher up. Ensure your permits are in order as they are checked at the Chhomrong checkpoint. Carry sufficient cash as there are no ATMs beyond Pokhara.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong down to the Modi Khola river and then up through bamboo and rhododendron forests to Dovan (2,600m) or Himalaya Hotel (2,920m). Pass through Sinuwa and enjoy dramatic gorge scenery. Approx 5-6 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Himalaya Hotel teahouse and rest. The trail narrows into a spectacular gorge with towering walls on either side. Explore the immediate surroundings and watch for mountain birds.
day_by_day.evening: The gorge creates an early dusk — enjoy the dramatic atmosphere. Warm up with hot drinks and rest well as altitude increases.

meals.breakfast: Muesli with hot milk and eggs at Chhomrong teahouse for NPR 400-600
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or noodle soup at Dovan teahouse for NPR 500-700
meals.dinner: Vegetable curry and rice at Himalaya Hotel teahouse for NPR 600-800

day_by_day.notes: This section of the trail passes through avalanche-prone areas — always check with local teahouse owners about current conditions. The trail can be slippery after rain. Trekking poles are highly recommended. Altitude begins to increase more rapidly from here.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Himalaya Hotel through Hinku Cave and Deurali (3,230m) to Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC) at 3,700m. The scenery becomes increasingly dramatic as the valley opens up. Approx 4-5 hours. Arrive at MBC and acclimatize.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest at MBC and allow your body to adjust to the altitude. Take short exploratory walks around the base camp area. The views of Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Peak, 6,993m) are awe-inspiring from here.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the alpenglow on the surrounding peaks as the sun sets. The silence and scale of the mountains at MBC is profound. Rest early and hydrate well.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and boiled eggs at Himalaya Hotel teahouse for NPR 500-700
meals.lunch: Hot soup and bread at Deurali teahouse for NPR 600-800
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or pasta at MBC teahouse for NPR 700-900

day_by_day.notes: Altitude sickness can affect trekkers at MBC. Watch for symptoms: headache, nausea, dizziness, loss of appetite. Drink 3-4 liters of water daily. Do not ascend further if you feel unwell. Diamox (acetazolamide) can help with acclimatization if prescribed by a doctor before the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning hike from MBC to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) at 4,130m — approximately 2-3 hours. Arrive at the iconic ABC amphitheater surrounded by Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Machhapuchhre, Gangapurna, and Glacier Dome. This is the highlight of the entire trek.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the ABC area, walk to the glacier edge, take photographs, and soak in the extraordinary 360-degree mountain panorama. The scale of the surrounding walls is humbling. Rest and acclimatize.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset paint the Annapurna massif in shades of gold and pink — one of the most memorable experiences in Himalayan trekking. Celebrate reaching ABC with fellow trekkers.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at MBC before departing — porridge and tea for NPR 600-800
meals.lunch: Hot noodle soup or fried rice at ABC teahouse for NPR 800-1000
meals.dinner: Celebratory dal bhat or pasta at ABC teahouse for NPR 800-1100

day_by_day.notes: Prices at ABC are significantly higher due to the remote location — budget accordingly. The temperature at ABC can drop well below freezing at night even in October. Wear all your layers. Sunrise at ABC the next morning is spectacular — set your alarm. Do not leave valuables unattended.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn for the spectacular ABC sunrise — watch the first light strike Annapurna I and cascade down the surrounding peaks. Take final photographs and begin the descent back to MBC and then to Deurali. Approx 3-4 hours descending.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue descending from Deurali back through the gorge to Himalaya Hotel or push further to Sinuwa. The descent is faster but harder on the knees — use trekking poles. Approx 4-5 hours total descent.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Sinuwa or Bamboo teahouse and rest. Enjoy the thicker air at lower altitude. Reflect on the incredible experience of ABC.

meals.breakfast: Hot tea and biscuits at ABC before sunrise, then porridge at MBC for NPR 600-800
meals.lunch: Soup and snacks at Deurali or Himalaya Hotel for NPR 600-800
meals.dinner: Dal bhat at Sinuwa or Bamboo teahouse for NPR 500-700

day_by_day.notes: Descending is harder on joints than ascending — take your time on steep sections. Knees can be strained significantly on the long descent. Trekking poles and knee supports are helpful. Stay hydrated even while descending.

day_by_day.morning: Continue descending from Sinuwa/Bamboo back to Chhomrong. Enjoy the returning views of Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre. Approx 3-4 hours. Arrive in Chhomrong and enjoy a hot shower and rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Trek from Chhomrong to Jhinu Danda (1,780m), a small village famous for its natural hot springs on the banks of the Modi Khola river. Approx 1.5-2 hours descent.
day_by_day.evening: Soak in the natural hot springs at Jhinu Danda — the perfect reward after days of trekking. The hot springs are set beside the rushing river with mountain views. Utterly relaxing.

meals.breakfast: Eggs and toast at Sinuwa teahouse for NPR 400-600
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at Chhomrong for NPR 500-700
meals.dinner: Vegetable curry and rice at Jhinu Danda teahouse for NPR 500-700

day_by_day.notes: The Jhinu Danda hot springs entry fee is approximately NPR 300-500. Bring a towel and change of clothes. The springs are open until around 6 PM. Jhinu Danda is a quieter, more peaceful stop than Chhomrong — enjoy the tranquility.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Jhinu Danda through New Bridge and along the Modi Khola valley back to Nayapul. The trail passes through terraced farmland, small villages, and riverside scenery. Approx 4-5 hours. Catch a jeep or bus back to Pokhara.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Pokhara by early afternoon. Check into your hotel, shower, and rest. Treat yourself to a massage at one of Lakeside's many affordable wellness centers (approx NPR 1000-1500 for a full-body massage).
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate completing the Annapurna Sanctuary Trek with a special dinner at a nicer Lakeside restaurant. Browse the night market for souvenirs and local crafts.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and tea at Jhinu Danda teahouse for NPR 350-500
meals.lunch: Snack at a trail teahouse or quick meal in Nayapul for NPR 300-500
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner at Moondance or Caffe Concerto — try grilled trout or Nepali set meal for NPR 900-1400

day_by_day.notes: Jeep from Nayapul to Pokhara costs approximately NPR 400-600 per person on a shared basis. Book a massage in advance as Lakeside wellness centers fill up quickly during peak season. Rehydrate and eat well to recover from the trek.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning in Pokhara. Optional sunrise hike to Sarangkot viewpoint (1,600m) for panoramic views of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges — a 1.5-hour hike or short taxi ride. Return for a leisurely breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Gupteshwor Mahadev Cave and Davis Falls (Patale Chhango) near Pokhara — fascinating natural features. Alternatively, rent a kayak or try stand-up paddleboarding on Phewa Lake. Visit the Barahi Jungle nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Pokhara — explore the Lakeside area, pick up last-minute souvenirs (Thangka paintings, pashmina scarves, handmade paper products), and enjoy a farewell dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full Western or Nepali breakfast at a Lakeside café — try shakshuka or Nepali breakfast set for NPR 500-800
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café — try a fresh salad and soup for NPR 500-700
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a rooftop restaurant overlooking Phewa Lake — try Nepali-fusion cuisine or momos with local Everest beer for NPR 1000-1500

day_by_day.notes: Davis Falls and Gupteshwor Cave entry costs approximately NPR 50-100 each. Sarangkot taxi costs approximately NPR 600-800 one way. Use this day to sort laundry, repack, and prepare for the return journey to Kathmandu. Back up your trekking photos.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Nepal — take a scenic morning walk along the Phewa Lake shore for quiet reflection. Visit a local bakery for fresh pastries and coffee. If time allows, visit the Bindabasini Temple, Pokhara's oldest and most sacred temple.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from Pokhara to Kathmandu via domestic flight (25 min, approx USD 80-120) or tourist bus (6-7 hours). Spend remaining time in Kathmandu exploring Thamel, visiting Boudhanath Stupa or Pashupatinath Temple if time permits.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Kathmandu at a rooftop restaurant in Thamel. Pack and prepare for departure. Reflect on an extraordinary 14-day Annapurna adventure.

meals.breakfast: Pastries and coffee at a Lakeside bakery in Pokhara for NPR 400-600
meals.lunch: Quick meal at Pokhara airport or Kathmandu upon arrival — try momo or thukpa for NPR 300-500
meals.dinner: Final dinner at a Thamel rooftop restaurant — try Newari cuisine or Tibetan dishes for NPR 800-1200

day_by_day.notes: Book your Pokhara-Kathmandu domestic flight well in advance as October is peak season and seats fill quickly. Mountain flights from Pokhara offer stunning aerial views of the Annapurna range on clear days. Allow at least 3 hours before any international departure from Kathmandu's Tribhuvan International Airport.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Annapurna, Nepal Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Annapurna Sanctuary, Annapurna Conservation Area Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from Kathmandu airport to your boutique stay in the Annapurna Conservation Area. En route, enjoy a scenic drive through the Himalayan foothills with a knowledgeable private guide providing cultural and geographical context. Stop at a panoramic viewpoint along the Prithvi Highway for first breathtaking views of the Annapurna massif.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into your boutique accommodation, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome orientation session with your dedicated trek coordinator. Sip locally sourced Himalayan herbal tea on the lodge terrace as the sun sets behind the peaks. Light acclimatization walk around the immediate lodge grounds.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Gourmet welcome spread at the lodge upon arrival — freshly baked Newari bread, organic local cheeses, seasonal fruit platters, and premium Nepali tea selection
meals.dinner: Private candlelit dinner at the lodge's signature restaurant featuring Dal Bhat Royale (slow-cooked lentils, saffron-infused rice, organic mountain vegetables, and tandoori chicken) paired with a curated selection of imported wines

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day — keep activities light. Stay well-hydrated to begin acclimatization. Your butler will unpack luggage and prepare a welcome amenity kit including altitude sickness tablets, electrolyte sachets, and premium skincare suited for mountain climate.

day_by_day.morning: Guided sunrise nature walk through the rhododendron and oak forests surrounding the lodge. Your naturalist guide will identify Himalayan bird species including the Danphe (Himalayan Monal, Nepal's national bird), eagles, and rare pheasants. Carry premium binoculars provided by the lodge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Introductory acclimatization hike to a nearby viewpoint offering panoramic views of Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, and Machapuchare (Fishtail Mountain). The trail is moderate and well-maintained, approximately 3–4 hours round trip with a private guide and a porter carrying your daypack and refreshments.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the lodge for a luxury mountain spa session — choose from a deep-tissue Himalayan salt stone massage or an Ayurvedic herbal oil treatment. Followed by a private stargazing session with a telescope set up by the lodge's astronomy guide.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet buffet breakfast on the terrace — Eggs Benedict with Himalayan black salt, fresh fruit bowls, house-made granola with yak milk yogurt, freshly squeezed juices, and Nepali filter coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet trail picnic prepared by the lodge chef — artisan sandwiches, organic salads, energy bars, dark chocolate, and thermos of hot soup served at the mountain viewpoint
meals.dinner: Multi-course Nepali tasting menu at the lodge — Tibetan butter soup, grilled mountain trout, slow-braised yak tenderloin with roasted root vegetables, and cardamom crème brûlée for dessert

day_by_day.notes: This is a gentle acclimatization day. Altitude gain is kept minimal. Drink at least 3–4 liters of water. Avoid alcohol on Day 2 to assist acclimatization.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning yoga and pranayama session on the lodge's open-air mountain deck led by a certified Himalayan yoga instructor. Practice breathing techniques specifically designed for high-altitude environments. Followed by a guided meditation session as the sun illuminates the Annapurna peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic hike to a traditional Gurung village near the sanctuary. Explore the village with a local cultural guide, visit a Buddhist monastery, spin prayer wheels, and interact with local artisans weaving traditional fabrics. Enjoy a private demonstration of Gurung traditional dance and music.
day_by_day.evening: Cultural immersion evening at the lodge — participate in a hands-on Nepali cooking class with the head chef, learning to prepare Momos (dumplings), Thukpa (noodle soup), and Sel Roti (rice doughnuts). Enjoy your creations as dinner.

meals.breakfast: Ayurvedic morning breakfast — warm turmeric milk, steamed buckwheat porridge with wild honey and mountain berries, poached eggs with herb-infused butter on sourdough toast
meals.lunch: Authentic Gurung village lunch hosted by a local family — traditional Dhido (buckwheat dough), fermented vegetables, smoked meat, and local raksi (millet wine) for those who wish
meals.dinner: Your own cooking class creations served in the lodge's private dining room, accompanied by premium Himalayan craft beer and local herbal digestifs

day_by_day.notes: Village visit requires modest dress — lodge will provide wraps if needed. Photography is welcome in the village but always ask permission before photographing residents.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for a full-day premium guided trek into the heart of the Annapurna Sanctuary. Begin ascending through dense bamboo and rhododendron forests on well-marked trails. Your head guide and two porters accompany you, carrying all gear and a gourmet picnic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue ascending toward the Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) approach trail, passing glacial moraines and high-altitude meadows. Stop at strategic rest points to photograph the towering walls of Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna III, Gangapurna, and the iconic Machapuchare. Wildlife spotting for Himalayan tahr, snow leopard tracks, and alpine birds.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at a premium high-altitude lodge or pre-arranged luxury tented camp with heated interiors, premium sleeping bags rated to -20°C, and private en-suite facilities. Warm up by the wood fire stove as your private cook prepares dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hearty high-energy breakfast — oatmeal with Himalayan honey, protein-rich egg scramble with yak cheese, whole grain toast, and a thermos of premium coffee to carry on trail
meals.lunch: Gourmet trail picnic at a scenic rest stop — smoked salmon wraps, quinoa salads, premium energy snacks, hot soup in a thermos, and artisan chocolate
meals.dinner: Three-course dinner at the high-altitude camp — hearty vegetable and lentil soup, slow-cooked mountain chicken with roasted potatoes and seasonal greens, and warm apple crumble with cream

day_by_day.notes: Today's trek is the most physically demanding so far. Altitude gain is significant — move at a slow, steady pace. Your guide will monitor for any signs of altitude sickness. Emergency oxygen is carried by the support team.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up call for the ultimate Annapurna Sanctuary sunrise experience. Trek to the optimal viewpoint to witness the golden alpenglow illuminating the entire Annapurna massif — a once-in-a-lifetime spectacle. Your guide will set up a premium spotting scope for close-up views of the glaciers and summit ridges.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely exploration of the sanctuary basin at your own pace. Optional short hike to the base of a glacier with your guide. Photography session with a professional mountain photographer provided by the lodge to capture your journey against the dramatic backdrop.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and recovery afternoon at the high-altitude camp. Enjoy hot stone foot baths prepared by your camp attendant. Journal writing, reading, or simply absorbing the profound silence of the Himalayan sanctuary. Evening bonfire (where permitted) under an extraordinary star-filled sky.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn hot chocolate and energy bars before sunrise hike, followed by a full cooked breakfast upon return — French toast with mountain berry compote, scrambled eggs, and freshly brewed coffee
meals.lunch: Light and nutritious lunch at camp — lentil soup, fresh flatbreads, hummus, roasted vegetables, and seasonal fruit
meals.dinner: Special celebration dinner at camp — Tibetan hot pot with premium cuts of yak meat, mountain vegetables, and noodles cooked at the table, paired with imported red wine

day_by_day.notes: Spend a full day at this altitude to maximize acclimatization before any further ascent. Drink consistently throughout the day. The professional photographer's images will be edited and delivered digitally as a premium trip memory package.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the descent from the sanctuary back toward lower elevations. The return trek reveals entirely new perspectives of the landscape as you descend through changing vegetation zones — from alpine scrub to dense rhododendron forest. Your guide shares botanical knowledge about the medicinal plants of the region.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back at the main lodge area. Enjoy a well-deserved luxury spa recovery session — full-body deep tissue massage, hot spring soak (if available locally), and a revitalizing Himalayan herbal facial treatment.
day_by_day.evening: Private documentary screening in the lodge's lounge — curated films about Annapurna's climbing history, local Gurung culture, and Himalayan ecology. Followed by a guided tasting of premium Nepali teas sourced from the Ilam region, hosted by a certified tea sommelier.

meals.breakfast: Energy-packed descent day breakfast — banana pancakes with maple syrup, Greek yogurt with granola and honey, fresh fruit, and premium coffee
meals.lunch: Trailside lunch at a scenic rest point — gourmet sandwiches, fruit, premium trail mix, and electrolyte drinks
meals.dinner: Elegant lodge dinner — roasted beet and goat cheese salad, pan-seared Himalayan trout with lemon caper butter and sautéed greens, followed by dark chocolate mousse with raspberry coulis

day_by_day.notes: Descending is easier on the lungs but harder on the knees. Trekking poles are recommended and provided by the lodge. Your porter will carry all heavy gear.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and leisure morning at the boutique lodge. Optional gentle yoga session, swimming (if pool available), or simply relaxing on the terrace with books from the lodge library. Complimentary laundry service handles all trekking gear.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided nature photography walk with a professional wildlife photographer. Explore the lodge's surrounding forests and meadows focusing on macro photography of alpine flora, fungi, and insects, as well as landscape composition techniques with the Annapurna range as backdrop.
day_by_day.evening: Private stargazing and astronomy session with a dedicated guide using high-powered telescopes. The Annapurna region's clear October skies offer extraordinary visibility of the Milky Way, planets, and deep-sky objects. Followed by a fireside storytelling session about Himalayan mythology and local legends.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely late breakfast — eggs any style, fresh pastries, seasonal fruit, yogurt parfaits, freshly squeezed juices, and your choice of premium teas or coffees
meals.lunch: Light garden lunch at the lodge — mezze platter, artisan cheeses, cold cuts, fresh salads, and sparkling water with local fruit infusions
meals.dinner: Chef's special seven-course tasting menu featuring the finest local and imported ingredients — amuse-bouche, soup, salad, sorbet, main course, cheese course, and dessert, paired with a curated wine flight

day_by_day.notes: This is a designated rest day. Guests are encouraged to do only what feels restorative. The lodge's wellness team is available for additional spa treatments by appointment.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive private helicopter excursion over the Annapurna massif. Depart from a nearby helipad for a 60–90 minute aerial tour providing bird's-eye views of Annapurna I through IV, Dhaulagiri, Machhapuchhre, and the entire sanctuary basin you trekked through. Land at a high-altitude viewpoint for photographs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from helicopter excursion. Afternoon visit to a traditional Magar or Gurung cultural heritage site with a specialist cultural anthropologist guide. Explore ancient stone architecture, visit a local shaman (Dhami) for a cultural demonstration, and browse handcrafted local textiles and jewelry.
day_by_day.evening: Private bonfire dinner under the stars at the lodge's outdoor terrace. Enjoy a Himalayan BBQ — marinated yak kebabs, tandoori chicken, grilled mountain vegetables, and freshly baked naan, accompanied by live acoustic Nepali folk music performed by local musicians.

meals.breakfast: Pre-flight light breakfast — croissants with butter and jam, fresh fruit, yogurt, and premium coffee to ensure comfort during the helicopter flight
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch at a heritage lodge or cultural center — traditional Nepali thali with premium ingredients, fresh salads, and local herbal drinks
meals.dinner: Himalayan BBQ bonfire dinner with imported wines, craft cocktails featuring local spirits, and a dessert of warm Gulab Jamun with saffron ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter excursion is weather-dependent. The lodge will monitor conditions from the previous evening and confirm the flight by 06:00. A backup scenic drive alternative is arranged in case of cancellation.

day_by_day.morning: Guided medicinal plant and ethnobotany walk with a local Ayurvedic practitioner. Learn how Himalayan communities have used plants for medicine, food, and ritual for thousands of years. Collect samples for a personalized herbal tea blend crafted for you to take home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Multi-day trek preparation or alternative: explore a different trail in the Annapurna Conservation Area leading to a high-altitude lake or waterfall. The trail offers diverse ecosystems — subtropical forest transitioning to temperate and subalpine zones with spectacular biodiversity.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private dinner experience — the lodge arranges a rooftop dinner under the open sky with the Annapurna peaks illuminated by moonlight. Personalized menu created by the head chef based on your dietary preferences, with premium wine pairing.

meals.breakfast: Wholesome breakfast — Nepali-style beaten rice (Chiura) with spiced potatoes, poached eggs, fresh fruit, and masala chai
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch enjoyed beside a mountain stream or waterfall — smoked salmon on rye, Caesar salad, premium cheese selection, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Rooftop private dinner — lobster bisque, pan-roasted duck breast with cherry reduction and truffle mashed potatoes, and a dessert of tiramisu with Himalayan espresso

day_by_day.notes: The ethnobotany walk moves slowly and covers short distances — suitable for all fitness levels. Bring a small notebook to record plant names and uses. Your personalized herbal tea blend will be packaged beautifully as a take-home gift.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise hike to a panoramic ridge viewpoint offering 360-degree views of the Annapurna range, Dhaulagiri, Manaslu, and on clear days, distant views toward Everest. Your guide carries a premium spotting scope and a thermos of hot coffee for the summit celebration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to lodge and participate in a private Thangka painting workshop with a master Tibetan Buddhist artist. Learn the sacred geometry and symbolism behind these intricate religious artworks. Create your own small Thangka to take home as a unique souvenir.
day_by_day.evening: Rejuvenating spa evening — begin with a traditional Nepali Panchkarma detox treatment, followed by a hot stone massage, and conclude with a private aromatherapy session using Himalayan essential oils. Retire early for a restful night.

meals.breakfast: Pre-hike light breakfast — energy bars, banana, and a thermos of premium coffee; full breakfast served upon return — eggs Benedict, fresh pastries, seasonal fruits, and juices
meals.lunch: Lodge poolside or terrace lunch — grilled paneer with herb salad, freshly baked flatbreads, hummus, and a selection of cold pressed juices
meals.dinner: Light and nourishing spa dinner — miso soup, sashimi-style Himalayan trout, steamed vegetables with sesame dressing, and green tea panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: The Thangka painting workshop requires patience and a steady hand — all materials are provided and the master artist guides every step. Your completed artwork is mounted and wrapped for safe transport home.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day premium trek to a remote and less-visited area of the Annapurna Conservation Area — chosen by your head guide based on current trail conditions and wildlife activity. Trek through pristine wilderness with minimal tourist traffic, offering an authentic wilderness experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reach a remote high-altitude meadow or ridge for lunch with unobstructed Himalayan views. Spend the afternoon exploring the area with your naturalist guide — tracking wildlife, identifying alpine flora, and soaking in the solitude of the high Himalayas.
day_by_day.evening: Return to lodge as the last light fades over the peaks. Enjoy a private Jacuzzi or hot bath drawn with Himalayan mineral salts and essential oils. Relaxed evening with a nightcap of premium aged rum or whisky by the fireplace.

meals.breakfast: High-energy trekking breakfast — oatmeal with nuts and dried fruit, protein-rich egg scramble, whole grain toast, and a thermos of coffee or tea
meals.lunch: Gourmet summit picnic — charcuterie board with premium meats and cheeses, artisan crackers, dark chocolate, and a thermos of hot tomato soup
meals.dinner: Comfort dinner at the lodge — French onion soup, slow-braised lamb shank with rosemary jus and roasted root vegetables, and warm sticky toffee pudding with vanilla ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Trail selection for this day will be finalized the evening before based on weather and conditions. This is one of the most rewarding days of the trip — pack your best camera gear.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure morning — sleep in, enjoy a late breakfast, and spend time reflecting on the journey. Optional: private journaling session on the terrace with a Himalayan sunrise view, guided by a mindfulness coach provided by the lodge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exclusive private river rafting or kayaking excursion on a nearby Himalayan river (subject to seasonal conditions and proximity). Alternatively, visit a local conservation project within the Annapurna Conservation Area — meet the rangers, learn about snow leopard and red panda conservation efforts, and contribute to a tree-planting initiative.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell cultural evening arranged by the lodge — a private performance of traditional Gurung and Magar dances in full ceremonial costume, followed by a blessing ceremony by a local Buddhist lama for safe travels. Receive a traditional Khata (white silk scarf) as a blessing.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent late breakfast — smoked salmon bagels, eggs royale, fresh pastries, premium coffee, and a Himalayan fruit smoothie bowl
meals.lunch: Riverside or conservation center lunch — packed gourmet boxes with sandwiches, salads, fruit, and premium snacks
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at the lodge — five-course celebration meal featuring the best of Nepali and international cuisine, with a premium champagne toast to the journey

day_by_day.notes: The conservation visit includes a donation component — the lodge coordinates a contribution on your behalf to the Annapurna Conservation Area Project (ACAP). A certificate of contribution is provided.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise moment at the lodge — wake before dawn for one last meditation or yoga session on the mountain terrace. Watch the Annapurna peaks turn gold in the morning light. Private photography session to capture your final morning in the sanctuary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the journey back toward Kathmandu via private luxury vehicle or chartered helicopter (depending on preference and budget). En route or upon arrival in Kathmandu, visit the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Boudhanath Stupa — walk the kora (circumambulation path) and light butter lamps for good fortune.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a luxury 5-star hotel in Kathmandu (Dwarika's Hotel or similar heritage property recommended). Enjoy the contrast of Kathmandu's vibrant culture after the serene mountain sanctuary. Explore the hotel's heritage courtyards and museum.

meals.breakfast: Final lodge breakfast — a grand spread of all your favorites from the past two weeks, prepared with care by the lodge kitchen team as a farewell gesture
meals.lunch: En route lunch at a premium roadside restaurant or in Kathmandu — Newari cuisine tasting platter including Bara, Yomari, Chatamari, and Aila (millet spirit)
meals.dinner: Dinner at one of Kathmandu's finest restaurants — Krishnarpan at Dwarika's Hotel (if staying there) offers an extraordinary multi-course traditional Nepali meal served in authentic silver and bronze vessels

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter transfer from the sanctuary to Kathmandu takes approximately 45 minutes and is highly recommended for the final aerial views of the Himalayas. Book in advance through the lodge concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Kathmandu — explore the Thamel district for premium souvenir shopping: hand-knotted carpets, pashmina shawls, singing bowls, Thangka paintings, and high-quality trekking gear. Your guide accompanies you to ensure authentic purchases at fair prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Pashupatinath Temple (UNESCO World Heritage Site) and Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple) for a final cultural and spiritual immersion in Nepal's extraordinary heritage. Private guide provides deep historical and religious context.
day_by_day.evening: Departure preparations — luxury hotel concierge handles all luggage and airport transfers. Enjoy a final Nepali farewell dinner at the hotel before your private airport transfer. Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport with ample time for your departure flight.

meals.breakfast: Lavish hotel breakfast buffet — international and Nepali options, fresh juices, pastries, eggs to order, and premium coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a rooftop café in Thamel — club sandwich, fresh salad, and a signature Himalayan cocktail or fresh lime soda
meals.dinner: Final farewell dinner at the hotel or airport lounge — curated Nepali and continental menu with a glass of premium champagne to celebrate an extraordinary 14-day Himalayan journey

day_by_day.notes: Ensure all permits, trekking certificates, and conservation area passes are collected as souvenirs. The lodge provides a beautifully bound trip journal with photographs, maps, and notes from your guides as a premium keepsake. Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for airport check-in.

query: Nepal trekking Annapurna, $2000 solo, October 2026, 14 days
